li: Live accompaniment for all graded classes
Faculty of nine, all former professionals
Member, International Association of Dance Medicine and Science
p: International Dance began in a rented church hall with eleven students and one upright piano. The piano is still here.
The studio grew because the teaching was honest. Dancers were told what was working and what was not, at an age when that still changes outcomes.
We remain independent, unaffiliated with any franchise or examination board that would dictate what our dancers are allowed to become.
Technique before tricks. A clean tendu at seven becomes a clean everything at seventeen.
We teach the Vaganova syllabus through the graded levels, with Cecchetti port de bras work layered in from level four.
Injury prevention is taught as part of class, not as a separate workshop after something has already gone wrong.
Studio A seats a full corps with room to travel. Studio B is intimate, built for pointe and pas de deux.
Both rooms have sprung subfloors, which is not a luxury but the difference between a twenty-year career and a five-year one.
Mirrors are curtained during creative work. Dancers should learn to feel a position before they learn to check it.
Graduates have joined companies in Hamburg, Montreal, Tokyo, and Cape Town.
Others have gone to university, to medicine, to architecture, and still take Thursday open class when they are in town.
